Their CDX digest RT4NWITA6FTWUBJGEMRVV6RT7UKFAVSB is the base-32 SHA-1 of the file acquired here, so these exact bytes have been published since at least 2012. The file page was captured on 2015-01-27, 2016-12-25 and 2025-06-29.

original_format: PNG, RGBA (alpha 255 everywhere), exactly two colours: #32FF32 green (6,236 px) and #000000 black (208,804 px)

transcription: HELLO, WORLD!        (inverse video: black text on a green bar)
visible_content.reading: Someone ran a five-line Hello World program (HOME cleared the screen, so the RUN command is gone), then typed LIST at the prompt. The screen is not a power-on or boot screen.

identification.software: Applesoft BASIC. Established: Apple's documentation defines ] as the Applesoft prompt and > as the Integer BASIC prompt, and HOME, INVERSE and NORMAL are Applesoft statements (evidence/source-excerpts.md, sections 3-4).
identification.hardware_model: Not established. Nothing on screen names a model. Uppercase-only text and the 40-column layout fit the Apple II, II Plus, and a IIe in uppercase mode alike.
identification.rom_or_emulator: Not established. The 560x384 two-colour raster is exactly the 280x192 Apple text screen doubled, which is typical of emulator output, but the page does not name an emulator, ROM set, or real hardware.
identification.boot_banner: Absent. An Autostart ROM cold start clears the screen and shows a machine-name banner top centre before BASIC starts (Apple II Reference Manual, 1979; OCR reads 'APPLE II'). No banner appears in this image.
identification.label_allowed_by_evidence: Applesoft BASIC prompt on an Apple II-family text screen (model and emulator unknown)
identification.label_not_supported: Apple II boot screen; Apple II Plus; any specific ROM revision
